next.name: LockBit Gang
next.headline: LockBit Gang: a ransomware-as-a-service crew hit by a 2024 police takedown but still talking of more attacks
next.in_short: LockBit is a ransomware group that has run since 2019 and is linked to thousands of attacks. Police seized its servers in February 2024. Its leader says the gang will keep going.

sentences.t: Analyst1 reports that the LockBit gang began operating in September 2019.
The catalogue record lists Bitwise Spider as an alias. CrowdStrike Intelligence tracks LockBit and Defray under names that include ALPHA SPIDER and BITWISE SPIDER.
Mandiant tracks the LockBit ransomware operator as UNC2758. It also tracks five other notable affiliate groups.
The group's public face is a persona called LockBitSupp. Law enforcement officials and cybersecurity experts believe the person behind it is Russian.
The Analyst1 author believes the gang's leader is behind the LockBitSupp persona. The author calls this an assessment, not established fact.

U.S. and British authorities identified Dmitry Khoroshev as the leader and charged him with 26 criminal counts. The U.S., U.K. and Australia have sanctioned him. The person behind LockBitSupp denies being Khoroshev and says police attached the wrong person to the alias.
LockBit has been linked to thousands of attacks in recent years, including attacks on hospital systems and critical infrastructure.
In 2022 the group attacked Canada's largest pediatric health center shortly before Christmas. A September attack on two New York hospitals forced them to divert ambulances.
Analyst1 says LockBit primarily extorted victims in the United States, Germany and France. Its victims also included a UK car company, an IT consulting firm and two airlines.
Analyst1 says LockBit got in by exploiting unpatched, vulnerable VPN software, and in one case by brute-forcing an administrative account.
CrowdStrike's OverWatch team observed two VPN-based LockBit affiliate intrusions between mid-2021 and mid-2022. In one case an affiliate tried to steal data with the StealBit tool.
Analyst1 says LockBit built StealBit itself and also used public tools such as Rclone to take data. It reports that the ransomware spreads over the SMB protocol.
Analyst1 reports that LockBit tried to recruit employees at target firms directly. It used DDoS as a third form of extortion only sparingly. It added a Linux/ESXi variant in October 2021.
CrowdStrike Intelligence observed ALPHA SPIDER using Cobalt Strike variants and SystemBC variants after breaking into ESXi servers in late 2022.
The catalogue record lists tools tied to the group. They include Mimikatz, PsExec, CrackMapExec and PowerShell Empire, alongside LockBit and LockBit Black.
Analyst1 says LockBit announced a major release, LockBit Black, in June 2022. In September 2022 the ransomware builder source code leaked.
Analyst1 says LockBit claimed a 2021 breach of Accenture. The author thinks the gang likely oversold it and that Accenture significantly downplayed what happened.

On November 9, 2022, Mikhail Vasiliev, a dual Russian-Canadian national, was accused over LockBit. The Analyst1 author believes the suspect is not a core member, so the arrest mattered less than media reported.
Mandiant reports that in June 2023 the U.S. Department of Justice announced criminal charges against a LockBit affiliate.

In February 2024 an international police operation, announced by the UK National Crime Agency on February 19, seized LockBit's platform, hacking tools, cryptocurrency accounts and source code. Red Canary describes the operation, called Operation Cronos, as a big win against LockBit.
The report on that operation says several people alleged to be linked to LockBit were arrested in Ukraine and Poland. It does not name the source of that claim.
After the takedown, LockBitSupp put up a barebones leak site that listed five companies. In an interview LockBitSupp said the gang is still planning attacks and aims to attack one million companies.
The U.S. Justice Department has offered a $10 million reward in the case.
Patch VPN software promptly and protect administrator accounts with strong, unique credentials.
Keep offline backups and monitor virtualization hosts, which are often poorly watched.
